seo.description: Walk Amezrou near Zagora: earthen architecture, the historic Jewish quarter and oasis village life.

name: Amezrou
hero_subtitle: Earthen lanes and the old Jewish quarter — a walkable heritage corner of the Zagora oasis.

info.entry_val: Free to walk; tips for guides

overview.title: Lanes of earth and memory
overview.p1: Amezrou (Amazrou) is the oasis village side of Zagora: narrow lanes, earthen walls and traces of the old Jewish quarter that once formed part of the town’s social fabric.
overview.p2: It is best on foot. A short walk gives more sense of daily Draa life than the main road strip. Local guides sometimes offer context for a tip.
overview.p3: Stay respectful in residential lanes and ask before photographing people or private doorways.

3.title: Best colour
3.desc: Warm light on palms and sand.

food.title: Food near Amezrou
food.p1: Plan meals in Zagora town or pack simple supplies for outings away from the centre.
food.li1: Tagines and simple plates in town.
food.li2: Carry water on every desert or mountain outing.
food.li3: Dates and snacks from the souk on market days.
food.li4: Camp dinners are set menus on overnight trips.
food.li5: Confirm restaurant hours in the quiet season.
food.p2: Cash is useful for small oasis stops.

q1.question: How far from the centre?
q1.answer: On the edge of the oasis — a short hop from central Zagora.

q2.question: Is a guide needed?
q2.answer: Not required; helpful for history of the mellah and ksars.

q3.question: How long?
q3.answer: One to two hours at a relaxed pace.

q4.question: Photography?
q4.answer: Be discreet and ask permission in residential areas.

q5.question: Combine with the souk?
q5.answer: Yes on market days for a fuller local morning.
